chapter: Tuba players and New Orleans bands
title: Funeral parade with Dave Bailey; Bailey's drumming and the union
summary: The interviewer asks about a Sunday funeral where Barbarin's band met Bailey's; Barbarin praises Bailey and says the players should join the union.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Oh yeah, well I was there the other day for Sonny Henry, you know. What about that Sunday, that day, what was it, was it a Sunday you told me about where you met Dave Bailey there on the church?

Yeah, that was Sunday morning, yeah, yeah. I enjoyed him. I enjoyed the session, you know, we played, it was an hour, just one hour, from Shakespeare's Park to Robertson Street, Robertson, Louisiana Avenue. Yeah, I know that church. Some church there, I mean. And both bands met up.
He's great, I think he's great. Well I always thought he was a great jazz drummer, I mean, years ago, when I first heard him. Of course he was playing long before I was, you know what I mean?
How old you suppose he is? Who was that?
Dave. Well I'd give Dave about 62, 63, something like that.
You bet he's older than that man?

Probably, most likely, yeah he could be. But he's got plenty of life, that guy's got some life. He's a good drummer, he's a good Dixieland drummer, and of course he don't get the chance, I mean, you know, no more, you know, because I guess, well, I don't know, I guess on the count he don't belong to the Union, you know. Maybe he'd get a better break if they all, I think they all should join the Union, because I think they've got a pretty good band, I mean, they get a lot of funerals. The society, they like to change bands, I mean, sometimes, you know what I mean, they don't like to get the same bands all the time. I think it would be nice if they would join the Union.
